what_happened.line: The School Committee heard the proposed FY24 school budget presentation, which split the increase between personnel and expense accounts.
The committee sent the bus transportation policy to the policy committee, with a hard deadline, a capacity limit, public outreach and no waiver of first reading.
The committee voted to post the chemical hygiene officer and social media administrator positions; one member abstained.
The committee passed a higher per diem for substitute nurses, accepted the personnel report and accepted donations.
The budget vote was scheduled for March 15th, followed by the finance committee and town meeting on May 6th.

why_it_matters: The FY24 school budget starts its path to the town meeting vote, and the budget discussion covered a salary reserve for negotiations, possible out-of-district tuition increases and expiring grants, any of which can move the school share of the town budget, mostly taxes.
The bus policy rewrite could change how transportation is offered to students, and it will return for readings before any change takes effect.
